assessment.nobel_worthiness: KPZ is the clean example I look for: one stochastic growth equation whose scaling exponents and Tracy-Widom-type fluctuation statistics define a universality class reaching well beyond interface growth (directed polymers, random matrices, integrable models). It gives a simple mechanism behind messy non-equilibrium behaviour, and the exact solutions linking it to random-matrix theory are close to my own work.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the 1986 equation; Parisi is not in the credited set (and already has a prize), so a Kardar-Zhang pairing is the theory core. Takeuchi's liquid-crystal turbulence experiments gave the first clean experimental confirmation of the predicted distributions. Credit for the exact solutions (Johansson, Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and others) lies outside the supplied names, so any configuration is somewhat incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1986. Experimental confirmation (2010-2011) and later replications are independent and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and the field is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Takeuchi or a mathematical-physics contributor best completes the triple is arguable.
Exclusion of Parisi and of the exact-solution authors leaves attribution open.
Experimental realisations in other systems vary in how cleanly they show KPZ statistics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of matter classified by band-structure invariants, with protected boundary states. The theory is clean and general, and it reorganised condensed-matter physics and fed many other fields. Importance and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the quantum spin Hall effect (2005). Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe/CdTe wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Hasan (3D work) are not in the supplied credit, so the set is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in 2D (2007) and 3D materials is solid and independent. The field is mature and a prize would be timely, though it follows the 2016 topological-phase prize.
uncertainties: Allocation between 2D and 3D topological insulators is unresolved.
Several key theorists are missing from the supplied names.
The 2016 prize partly overlaps in subject, which may weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a simple geometric knob into flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model explains the magic angle with a transparent mechanism, and the discovery opened moire materials as a platform for correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands (2011). Cao, Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers observed correlated insulators and superconductivity (2018). Cao is not in the supplied names, and credit within the experimental group and for earlier twistronics ideas (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) is a live question.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the main phenomena, but the origin of the superconductivity is still debated and the field is moving quickly. Recognition may come slightly early, though the breadth of the field is considerable.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not settled.
Credit for earlier theory and for the junior experimental lead is complicated.
Sample-dependent behaviour suggests the field is still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, so one can study many-body physics directly: the superfluid-Mott transition, Fermi-Hubbard models and quantum gas microscopy. This is statistical mechanics made controllable, which I find appealing.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation. Greiner, Bloch and Hansch observed the Mott transition (2002), and Greiner built the microscopes. Esslinger's fermionic work is a fourth strong claim, so the supplied names force a choice among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller and Esslinger.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature and independently reproduced in many groups. Recognition is timely, although earlier BEC (2001) and optical-tweezer prizes are partly adjacent.
uncertainties: Choice among four strong contributors; Jaksch is missing from the supplied names.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links the foundations of quantum mechanics (no-cloning, entanglement) to security that does not depend on computational assumptions. BB84 and E91 are simple ideas with large downstream influence in quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84 (1984); Ekert proposed the entanglement-based E91 protocol (1991). Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the supplied names and would need discussion.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrations and satellite links exist, and the 2022 prize touched related foundations. Practical security against real-world side channels is still developing, though the underlying ideas are well established.
uncertainties: Prize category is borderline between physics and information science.
Wiesner's precedence is unresolved.
Practical QKD security and usefulness are debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is a controlled infinite-dimension limit that gives a non-perturbative, tractable account of the Mott transition and correlated metals, and it is now a standard tool for real materials. It is a general mechanism-based method with large influence.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit (1989), and Georges and Kotliar built the mapping to an impurity problem (1992). Metzner, Krauth and Rozenberg also deserve consideration, and the three supplied names do not cover all contributors.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature and widely validated against experiment and numerics. Its accuracy for finite-dimensional systems is an approximation, which some may regard as a limitation.
uncertainties: Credit among Metzner, Vollhardt, Georges, Kotliar and others is unsettled.
Exactness is limited to infinite dimension; finite-dimensional accuracy varies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture treats the onset of rigidity in disordered packings as a critical phenomenon with scaling and universal features, tying together glasses, granular matter, foams and emulsions. This is the kind of simple universal mechanism I value, and it overlaps with my soft-matter interests.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram (1998), and O'Hern, Silbert, Langer and Wyart contributed the quantitative critical-point picture. The two-person credit is clear on the conceptual proposal, but the quantitative theory depended on others.
assessment.maturity: Simulation and experimental support is substantial, but the nature of the transition and its relevance to real finite-temperature glasses are still debated. Recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Relevance of jamming to the glass transition is unresolved.
Quantitative critical-point contributors are not included in the supplied names.
Experimental tests are harder than for clean systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are central to precision metrology, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. The conceptual step is clean and the impact long-lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice (2001-2003), and Ye led much of the demonstrated accuracy gains. The two-person credit is reasonably clean, though the 2005 prize already honoured Ye's comb work with Hall and Hansch.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation exists in many labs, and a redefinition of the second is under discussion. The field is mature, although a clock prize may seem close to earlier metrology prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
Competing clock approaches (ions, thorium nuclear clock) bear on timing.
